name: Issue resolution desk
description: A config-driven, repo-agnostic issue-resolution desk with a shared workflow sandbox across four phases — Advise (planner explores the issue and writes .desk/plan.md), Execute (implementer follows the plan, dedupes open PRs, fixes the issue, and waits for CI), Grade (reviewer grades the change, posts PR comments, and writes structured .desk/grade.json), and Dream (retrospective appends durable lessons to .desk/memory.md for the next round). A GitHub issue (bound to a task by the github sync) flows through pre-checks, then the advisor plans; if the plan flags NEEDS_HUMAN the desk pauses in the same run for a human plan review (a round-keyed approval gate — Approve proceeds, Request changes replans with the feedback) while the shared sandbox hibernates. The implementer resolves the issue on the persistent workspace — adopting an existing open PR when one already resolves the issue, or opening tale/<id> — then the reviewer grades and a toolless LLM judge reads the structured grade to decide merge-readiness. Every judge verdict routes through one Dream retrospective, then: wrong_approach replans (bounded), approval parks at In review, needs-work loops Execute → Grade → Judge (bounded). All three loops share config.variables.maxReworkLoops (default 3). Cross-phase state lives in .desk/ on the shared workspace; each agent's METHOD lives in its agent config — step instructions carry only per-run context. Every visible step carries ui/role annotations so the generic operator workspace renders it with no per-vertical UI code.

steps.name: Do we have the issue coordinates?

config.description: The pre-check needs owner/repo/issue_number to call get_issue. A task with a malformed or non-GitHub external ref (nothing parsed) skips straight to the normal flow, where the implementer derives the repo from the issue URL itself — so a bad ref never hard-fails the run.

If the issue is still open, run the normal resolve → review flow. If it is ALREADY closed (merged, fixed elsewhere, won't-fix, duplicate) there is nothing for the desk to do — skip the whole implement/review loop (saving the implementer + reviewer sandbox spend) and mark the task done.

parameters.comment: [automated] GitHub issue #{{input.issueNumber}} is already closed upstream — nothing for the desk to resolve. Marking this task done.

steps.name: Did the advisor produce a plan?

config.description: A sandbox step always returns the success port; the real verdict is in output.data.ok. A failed advisor run (timeout, crash) must not flow into Execute with a synthesized summary and no plan — return the task to To do instead.

steps.name: Advisor failed — roll back to To do

parameters.comment: [automated] The advisor could not produce a plan for this issue: {{steps.advise.output.data.error || steps.advise.output.data.summary || 'no output'}} — returned to To do.

steps.name: Does the plan need a human?

config.description: When the advisor flags NEEDS_HUMAN in the plan summary, pause the run for a human plan review (same execution, shared sandbox) instead of ending the workflow.

Bounds the human plan-review loop with the same configurable cap as the rework loops. The round is bumped BEFORE this gate (variables.* only exists once a set_variables step wrote it), so the read here is always seeded. Within budget, request a FRESH round-keyed review; once exhausted, park at In review for manual takeover.

parameters.question:
The advisor flagged ambiguity in the plan (review round {{variables.planReviewRound}}/{{config.maxReworkLoops}}). Approve to proceed with implementation, or request changes with guidance.

{{steps.advise.output.data.summary}}

config.description: After the human responds, the engine re-executes the review step, which returns the recorded decision for THIS round (the request is idempotent per execution+step+round, so a later round always mints a fresh gate). Approve proceeds to implementation; Request changes captures the feedback into a variable (advise runs EARLIER in step order, so it cannot template this step's output directly) and replans.

steps.name: Store plan review feedback for replanning
Plan review rounds exhausted — park for a human

parameters.comment:
[automated] The plan is still ambiguous after {{config.maxReworkLoops}} human review rounds — a human should take over from here.

{{steps.advise.output.data.summary}}

steps.name: Implementer resolves the issue & opens/updates the PR

config.description: A sandbox step always returns the success port; the real verdict is in output.data.ok. Stop if the implementer failed to push a verified fix + PR.

steps.name: Implementer failed — roll back to To do

parameters.comment: [automated] The implementer could not resolve this issue: {{steps.execute.output.data.error || steps.execute.output.data.summary || 'no output'}} — returned to To do.

steps.name: Reviewer grades the change & comments on the PR
Did the reviewer produce a grade?

config.description: A sandbox step always returns the success port; the real verdict is in output.data.ok. A failed grade run (timeout, crash) must not reach the judge — it would decide from an empty grade and could burn a full replan loop on a guess. The implementation and PR exist, so park for a human instead.

steps.name: Reviewer failed — park for a human

parameters.comment: [automated] The reviewer could not grade the change: {{steps.grade.output.data.error || steps.grade.output.data.summary || 'no output'}} — the pull request is left open with the latest implementation; a human should review it. Moving to In review.

config.name: merge-judge
config.systemPrompt:
You are a strict merge gate for a code-review desk. You are given ONLY the reviewer's structured grade JSON for a proposed fix. Decide merge-readiness from it alone — you have no tools and no other context. Reply with EXACTLY two lines and nothing else:
severity: merge_ready|minor_fix|major_rework|wrong_approach
verdict: yes|no

Use severity merge_ready only when the grade reports no blocking problems and CI/tests are green. Use wrong_approach when the fundamental approach is unsound and replanning is needed. Use minor_fix or major_rework with verdict no when more implementation work is required. Use verdict yes only for merge_ready severity.

steps.name: Dream — capture lessons for the next round

run.instructions:
The merge judge ruled on issue #{{input.issueNumber}} ('{{input.task.title}}'). Judge verdict (severity + yes/no):
{{steps.judge.output.data}}

Rework loops so far: {{variables.reworkCount || 0}}/{{config.maxReworkLoops}}; replans so far: {{variables.replanCount || 0}}/{{config.maxReworkLoops}}.

Follow your standing method: read all files under /user/workspace/.desk/ (especially grade.json), append durable lessons to .desk/memory.md matched to this verdict — why the approach failed and what to avoid on wrong_approach, what failed review and the patterns to fix on a send-back, what worked plus repo/CI traps worth remembering on an approval — and write /user/output/summary.md listing what you appended.

config.description: When the judge's severity is wrong_approach, the desk sends the run back to Advise for a fresh plan instead of looping Execute with the same approach. Evaluated AFTER the shared Dream step (step outputs are persisted, so the routing can trail the retrospective).

Bounds the judge's wrong_approach → Advise replan loop the same way rework_gate bounds Execute rework — without it a judge that keeps ruling wrong_approach would loop Advise+Execute+Grade (burning their budgets each round) until the workflow timeout. Within budget, replan; once exhausted, escalate to a human.

steps.name: Replan limit reached — park for a human

parameters.comment: [automated] The desk reached its replan limit ({{config.maxReworkLoops}} replans; used {{variables.replanCount}}) — the judge keeps ruling the approach unsound. The latest attempt and review feedback are on the pull request — a human should take it over from here. Moving to In review.

config.description: The judge replies with two lines (severity + a yes/no verdict); jexl `in` does substring, and neither a 'no' verdict nor any severity word (merge_ready, minor_fix, major_rework, wrong_approach) contains 'yes', so this never false-approves. If yes, park for human merge; otherwise count a rework and loop back to the implementer.

parameters.comment: [automated] 🎯 The desk reviewed and approved this change — the pull request is ready for a human to merge. Rework loops: {{variables.reworkCount || 0}}/{{config.maxReworkLoops}}.{{(variables.reworkCount || 0) == 0 ? ' First-pass approval.' : ''}}

config.description: Bounds the grade → execute rework loop. reworkCount (workflow variables) counts how many times the reviewer has sent the change back; allow up to config.variables.maxReworkLoops reworks (default 3, adjustable per deployment). While within budget, loop back to the implementer with the latest feedback; once exhausted, escalate to a human instead of looping until the workflow timeout.

steps.name: Rework limit reached — park for a human

parameters.comment: [automated] The desk reached its rework limit ({{config.maxReworkLoops}} loops; used {{variables.reworkCount}}) without the reviewer approving the change. The pull request is left open with the latest attempt and the review feedback — a human should take it over from here. Moving to In review.
